Rules and supporting detail

Two paths meet in one report

Release path
Commit + build
→
Published version
Data path
Source records
→
Warehouse output
→
Reporting model
↓Visible reportUses the published application and the refreshed reporting model

The release path moves code into the running application. The data path moves source records through transformations and into a reporting model. The report depends on both, but either can advance while the other stays unchanged.

A successful build proves that an artifact was produced. A successful refresh proves that a process finished. Neither alone proves that the intended row, date, or business rule reached the report.

What proves the result

ClaimCheck the actual object
The change is deployedRunning version matches the intended commit
The source is currentExpected records and source timestamps are present
The rule produced the right rowsWarehouse output matches a known input and rule
The report is currentModel refresh includes that output and the visible report agrees
Why a green status can be misleading

A job can successfully process an old input. A model can successfully refresh the wrong partition. Verify a concrete expected record through the affected path, preserving its identity and relevant timestamps.
